config.layout.autoHideSideBar: Close the side bar when you open a file or a terminal. auto turns this on for a phone, in either orientation, and off for a tablet. Pick on or off here to decide for yourself.
walkthrough.title: Get Started with VSCodroid
walkthrough.description: Set up your mobile development environment
walkthrough.theme.title: Choose your theme
walkthrough.theme.description:
Pick a color theme that suits your style.

[Browse Color Themes](command:workbench.action.selectTheme)
walkthrough.folder.title: Open your project
walkthrough.folder.description:
Open a folder from your phone's storage, such as Documents or Download. Files that other apps saved in it show up too.

[Open Folder from Device](command:vscodroid.openFolderFromDevice)
walkthrough.run.title: Run your code
walkthrough.run.description:
Open a file and tap the play button in the editor's title bar. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Java, C, C++ and shell files run in a terminal.

Ruby, Java and C/C++ install on demand, and the button offers them when they are missing.

[Manage Toolchains](command:vscodroid.manageToolchains)
walkthrough.tools.title: Your development tools
walkthrough.tools.description:
VSCodroid comes with everything you need to start coding:

$(check) **Node.js** + npm: ready

$(check) **Python** + pip: ready

$(check) **Git**: ready

$(check) **make**: ready

**Java 21**, **Ruby** and **C/C++** install on demand. Touch and hold the VSCodroid icon on your home screen and pick **Manage toolchains**.

[Got It](command:vscodroid.welcome.toolsDismissed)
walkthrough.terminal.title: A powerful terminal
walkthrough.terminal.description:
Open a full bash terminal with every bundled tool on PATH: ``node``, ``python3``, ``git``, ``npm``.

``node -e 'console.log("hi")'`` prints ``hi``

``python3 -c 'print("hi")'`` prints ``hi``

``git init demo`` prints ``Initialized empty Git repository``

[Open Terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)
walkthrough.extensions.title: Extend with more features
walkthrough.extensions.description:
Install extensions from the Open VSX marketplace for language support, themes, and tools.

Extensions written in JavaScript work. The few that bundle a program compiled for desktop Linux can install without complaint and then do nothing, with no error on screen.

[Browse Extensions](command:workbench.view.extensions)
